Overall, KNN performed best across all models, achieving an R² of 0.8172 and MSE of 0.0128 in the final 11-feature set.
explanation_full:
The incremental feature analysis table demonstrates how the performance metrics (R² and MSE) for various models change as features are added sequentially. For the KNN model, the best performance was observed at 9 features (VFA -> Butyrate -> Acetate -> VSS -> Propionate -> Ethanol -> COD-O -> pH -> ORP_Low), achieving an R² of 0.8301 and an MSE of 0.0119. This suggests that the inclusion of the ORP_Low feature significantly boosted KNN's performance. 

Comparing the final 11-feature set, KNN maintained its strong performance with an R² of 0.8179 and an MSE of 0.0128. While the performance slightly dipped from the 9-feature set, it remained superior to all other models (RF: R²=0.7855, MSE=0.0150; XGBoost: R²=0.7478, MSE=0.0177). 

In summary, KNN is the best performing model, and the feature set including the first 9 features provides the optimal balance of high performance and feature count for KNN.
